messages:
Alex: Quick PSA — RC cutover in ~4h. Please double-check your changelog entries before the cutoff. We need them compact and lint-clean: one-line summary, component tag, and PR link. Example: ```Improve KV cache warmup [runtime] (#6123)```

Maria: Thanks. My PR has a long paragraph describing the rationale — should I keep it?

Alex: Keep the one-liner in the changelog. If you want, add a 1-sentence parenthetical for context, but avoid long prose — that breaks the release digest.

Jen: Also please add a component tag (brackets) — that feed powers per-team rollups. If you're unsure which tag, pick the closest (serving, runtime, infra, console, docs).

Dave: Is there a handy copyable template we can drop into PR descriptions?

Alex: Yep, paste this into the PR template's changelog section: ```{one-line summary} [{component}] (#{PR number})``` Example: ```Reduce model load latency [serving] (#7430)```

Maria: Cool, I'll trim mine and push a new commit.

release-bot: changelog-lint: running checks on submission #7430... 
release-bot: changelog-lint: violation found — missing component tag on PR #7430. See https://ci.internal/reports/7430

Dave: I'll take the lint fix for #7430.

Jen: Small reminder: the release manager will be doing a manual pass 30m before cutover. If lint is green, you're fine. If it errors, ping me here so I can triage.

Alex: One more nit — use present tense and avoid internal-only abbreviations. E.g., use "Improve latency" not "improved perf in prod".

Maria: Updated and pushed. New changelog line: ```Improve KV cache warmup [runtime] (#7430)```

release-bot: changelog-lint: all checks passed for #7430 :white_check_mark:

Jen: Nice — thanks. Everyone else, last call to finish edits in the next 45m. If you're blocked on the template, DM me. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Alex: Appreciate it — small, tidy entries make release notes readable for customers and SRE oncall. :thumbsup:

Dave: On it, squashing a tiny docs change and adding the one-liner now.

Maria: Thanks team, done.

Alex: Closing the thread when we cut.
